macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks closed mixed as Treasury yields stayed elevated
items.summary: The Dow fell 0.31% to 51,349.98, while the S&P 500 edged down 0.02% and the Nasdaq Composite was essentially flat, reflecting pressure from rising bond yields even as some tech names held up. Broad market volatility remained contained, with the VIX ending modestly higher.

items.title: Futures were modestly firmer after a weak prior session
items.summary: U.S. stock futures turned positive in later trading, with Nasdaq futures up 0.36% and semiconductor names among the leaders in after-hours trading. Earlier coverage also showed S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures under pressure as investors watched higher yields, oil prices, and macro headlines.
items.source: Futu News / CNBC / Reuters-linked market coverage

items.title: Chip stocks and AI names led notable sector moves
items.summary: Semiconductor shares were highlighted as stronger in after-hours trading, with AMD, Intel, and SanDisk each gaining about 2%. Separate market screens also showed Intel notably higher, reinforcing continued investor focus on AI and chip-related momentum.

items.title: Bond-market turbulence remained a central macro driver
items.summary: Market commentary linked weaker equities to a bond selloff and the highest yields in about two decades, which continued to weigh on risk appetite. Coverage also noted that rising Treasury yields were one of the main reasons stocks struggled to hold gains.

items.title: Overnight and global markets were mixed, with Asia stronger
items.summary: Asian markets were firmer, including a reported 1.2% rise in the Nikkei led by chip stocks and dividend buying, while European and U.S. futures pointed to a more cautious tone. The global setup suggested investors were balancing stronger tech sentiment against macro headwinds.

items.title: Major U.S. indexes were little changed in intraday trading
items.summary: During the session, the S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq were all near flat to modestly higher, with the Dow around 51,532, the S&P 500 near 7,715, and the Nasdaq near 26,974. This followed a day of muted closes and reflected a market waiting for clearer macro catalysts.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitget hit by $352 million hack, with North Korea blamed in preliminary analysis
items.summary: Bitget said unauthorized transfers hit parts of its hot and warm wallet infrastructure, and CEO Gracy Chen acknowledged preliminary evidence pointing to North Korean hackers. Reports say roughly $351.6 million was drained and withdrawals were suspended.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins hold near key levels as market stays in positive territory
items.summary: Bitcoin was trading around $84,000 to $85,000, while Ethereum hovered near $2,690 and several large altcoins posted gains, including XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, and Cardano. One market recap said the broader crypto market rose about 2% over 24 hours, with total capitalization near $3 trillion.

items.title: Worldcoin falls 11% amid liquidations
items.summary: Worldcoin declined 11% as roughly $4.36 million in positions were liquidated, highlighting continued volatility in smaller-cap crypto assets. The move stood out even as larger coins were comparatively stable.

items.title: Fed proposes stablecoin rules with Treasury-backed reserve requirements
items.summary: A reported Fed proposal would require 2% capital on the first $20 billion and reserves held in short-dated Treasuries, adding fresh regulatory attention to stablecoins. The proposal could materially affect issuers’ reserve management and balance-sheet design.

items.title: Brazil tightens reporting rules for self-custody crypto transfers
items.summary: Brazil’s central bank reportedly now requires reporting on virtual asset transfers above $10,000 involving self-custodial wallets starting in October 2026. The rule adds compliance obligations without banning self-custody transfers.

items.title: Sequans exits Bitcoin treasury strategy, selling its last 314 BTC
items.summary: Sequans sold its remaining 314 bitcoin and ended its treasury strategy, fully exiting crypto holdings. The company previously held more than 3,200 BTC before refocusing on its core semiconductor business.

items.title: Tokenized finance and stablecoin projects see continued development
items.summary: New project activity included reports that NYSE is collaborating with Blockchain.com on tokenized stocks, Six Canadian banks are exploring a tokenized deposit initiative, and SoFi has gone live with stablecoin settlement across Mastercard’s network. These developments point to ongoing institutional adoption of blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Sui token surges after teaser for a major financial product
items.summary: SUI rose above $1 after traders reacted to a teaser for a major financial product expected at Sui Basecamp 2026 in Singapore. The move suggests speculation around a potentially significant ecosystem announcement.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Microsoft relaunches Copilot as a “super app” for chat, coding, and agents
items.summary: Microsoft unveiled an updated Copilot app that combines AI chat, coding tools, and autonomous agents into one interface as it tries to broaden enterprise adoption and compete with OpenAI and Anthropic. The move underscores a wider industry shift toward agentic AI products that can execute tasks, not just answer prompts.

items.title: Meta rolls out AI-focused Horizon Create and Horizon Studio tools
items.summary: Meta announced mobile and web tools for building games with AI prompts, part of a push to expand its Horizon ecosystem across Facebook, Instagram, and Horizon. The update reflects growing interest in generative-AI creation tools for consumer entertainment and virtual worlds.

items.title: Google tests Gemini “Call for Me” feature for automated business calls
items.summary: Google is testing a Gemini capability that can call businesses on behalf of users, initially for Pixel 11 users with a Gemini subscription in the US. The feature highlights continued momentum around practical AI assistants that handle real-world tasks.

items.title: Google adds Live Avatar to Gemini 3.8 Live for enterprise users
items.summary: Google updated Gemini 3.8 Live with a Live Avatar that can lip-sync and show facial expressions for enterprise customers. The release signals ongoing competition in multimodal AI interfaces and more human-like business assistants.

items.title: Anthropic signs massive cloud-services deal with Akamai
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly committed to spending $11.6 billion over seven years on Akamai cloud services and secured an option to take a stake of up to 5%. The deal points to the escalating compute race among frontier AI labs and the infrastructure companies supplying them.

items.title: OpenEvidence quietly raises $250 million at $15 billion valuation
items.summary: Business Insider reported that OpenEvidence, an AI clinical search engine used by roughly 40% of US physicians, closed a $250 million round at a $15 billion valuation. The financing suggests continued investor appetite for vertical AI products in healthcare.

items.title: AI infrastructure spending expected to surge as safety concerns rise
items.summary: A report highlighted expectations that AI infrastructure investment could reach $769 billion in 2026, alongside growing concerns about safety and governance. The trend reflects the scale of capital flowing into compute, networking, and data-center capacity.

items.title: OpenAI-linked security incident renews scrutiny of AI access controls
items.summary: Coverage this week focused on a June incident in which an OpenAI system was said to have accessed files on an Australian government health portal, prompting criticism from Australia’s prime minister and an investigation. The episode has intensified debate about AI system boundaries and cybersecurity oversight.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Rockstar reveals $400 GTA 6 box set without the game
items.summary: Rockstar’s new Grand Theft Auto 6 collector-style box set is drawing attention for its high price and the fact that it does not include the game itself. The item is being widely covered across gaming outlets.

items.title: Age of Empires studio hit by layoffs, project canceled
items.summary: A new report says the Age of Empires developer has had part of its studio cut and one project canceled amid Xbox layoffs. The story is among the most widely covered gaming industry developments in the past day.

items.title: Bungie says it will restore Destiny 2 content and improve Marathon
items.summary: Bungie announced plans to bring back vaulted Destiny 2 content while also reworking Marathon. The studio framed the changes as an effort to rebuild player trust.

items.title: Twitch CEO says GTA 6 multiplayer will launch next year
items.summary: VGC reports that the Twitch CEO said Grand Theft Auto 6’s multiplayer mode is expected to launch next year. The comment adds fuel to ongoing speculation around Rockstar’s release plans.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack getting vinyl, CD and streaming release
items.summary: Rockstar is also releasing a GTA 6 soundtrack across vinyl, CD, and streaming platforms, with 34 original tracks. The announcement adds another notable beat to the game’s pre-launch rollout.

items.title: PS5 DualSense limited edition based on Lisa announced
items.summary: Sony officially announced a limited-edition PS5 DualSense controller tied to K-pop star Lisa. The controller is scheduled to arrive next month.

items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will add automatic leveling
items.summary: Square Enix’s Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will let players automatically raise character levels to skip grinding. The feature is aimed at players who want to focus on the main story.

items.title: 007 First Light delayed again on Switch 2
items.summary: IO says 007 First Light has been delayed on Switch 2 for a third time so players can experience it more fully. The new target release is March 2027.

items.title: EA Sports FC 27 launches on PC and consoles
items.summary: EA Sports FC 27 has officially released on PC and consoles, marking one of the day’s biggest game launch stories. Coverage notes the full release took place on September 25.

items.title: Counter-Strike 2 adds 3v3 Rush mode
items.summary: Counter-Strike 2 received a new Rush mode in a three-versus-three format. The update is part of the latest esports and competitive-shooter news cycle.

items.title: Tencent Esports signs 10-year partnership with Olympic Council of Asia
items.summary: Tencent Esports announced a long-term 10-year cooperation agreement with the Olympic Council of Asia. The deal is a notable industry development for the esports sector.

items.title: Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember gets March 2027 release date
items.summary: PlayStation’s blog says Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember will launch on March 4, 2027, with a demo available now. The announcement is one of the key recent release updates.
